label: D1 after a2->S1 rewarded; larger if trial before rewarded and policy leans a2
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S1 r") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * choice
explanation: Fires almost only at D1 right after a rare rewarded trial a2 -> S1 (zero at GO/D2 and after every other pattern; the previous-trial indicator alone gives test R^2 ~0.55 beyond timing). Magnitude within those D1 steps: roughly doubled when the trial before was also rewarded (tv reward -2 == 1; observed-only two-term model test R^2 0.66), and higher when the models D1 policy logit a1-a2 (choice) is less a1-leaning (negative weight; adds ~0.12, test R^2 0.78 with 3 terms). Choice is a model-internal quantity, not future. Earlier-trial S1 rewards, a1 S1 r streaks, value and hidden good state add nothing. Ceiling all = 0.60 (additive tables), which this exceeds via the interactions.

issues: The scores reproduce on test: the indicator alone gives 0.523, the observed-only two-term model 0.663, the indicator plus choice 0.760, and all three terms 0.784. The numbers are right, but the label points at the wrong trigger.

The feature does not fire only after a2->S1 rewarded. It also fires after a1->S1 rewarded whenever the D1 policy leans toward a2. Adding (phase==D1)*last_is('a1 S1 r')*(choice<0) to the three terms gives that term a weight of +0.95 (about the same size as the main effect) and raises test R^2 to 0.802. The worst-fit windows from misses show this directly: D1 values of 0.9-1.3 after a1 S1c r streaks late in the episode (t57-59, t92-93, t96, t98), all predicted at about 0.05. The explanation's line that 'a1 S1 r streaks added little' only holds for terms that ignore the policy.

One term covering both cases beats the claimed 3-term model: (phase==D1)*(prev_state==1)*(prev_reward==1)*np.maximum(1.5-choice,0) scores dev 0.794 / test 0.797. With the 1-choice version as the base, adding last_is('a2 S1 r') (test 0.7927 vs 0.7925) or the S1-reward x tv('reward',-2)==1 term (0.7931) adds almost nothing. So the claim that the activation 'roughly doubles when the trial before was rewarded' is mostly a stand-in for the policy logit. It only matters in the observed-only model (0.66), and the policy-based model makes it redundant.

The rare transition (a2) is not the cause. What matters is that S1 was rewarded while the policy has not yet moved toward a1. After a2->S1 rewarded the policy usually still leans a2, which is why the a2-specific label works most of the time.

After the unified term, misses shows no large systematic error class. The remaining errors are a uniform offset of about -0.03 to -0.04 at D1 and isolated first-trial-in-window D1 steps where the previous trial is outside the window ('?').
skeptic.revised_label: D1 after an S1-rewarded trial (either choice) while the policy still leans away from a1. Size grows as logit(a1)-logit(a2) falls. Mostly seen after a2->S1 rewarded. Observed-only proxy (rare a2->S1 rewarded, larger if trial before rewarded): test 0.66.
